title: Uniform sample mean concentration
statement: Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set equipped with a measurable space in which every singleton is measurable, and let $g:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ take values in $[-1,1]$. For a positive integer $m$ and $\\varepsilon\\ge0$, choose uniformly an $m$-tuple of elements of $\\Omega$. The probability that the empirical mean of $g$ on this tuple differs from the uniform expectation of $g$ on $\\Omega$ by at least $\\varepsilon$ is at most $2\\exp(-m\\varepsilon^2/2)$.
